newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Nov primary deficit at 952 million reais.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Nov primary deficit at 952 million reais.

text.p: Brazil's National Treasury posted a 952 million reais primary deficit for the federal government in the month of November, the Finance Ministry said.

November's figure reduced to 2.5 billion reais the federal government's primary surplus for the January-November period, down from 3.3 billion reais in the same period last year, the ministry said in a statement. The primary surplus in the first 11 months of the year was equivalent to 0.37 percent of gross domestic product, down from 0.56 percent in the January-November period last year, it said.

The ministry's statement attributed half of November's primary deficit to the social security system, which required an injection of 458 million reais mainly to pay a traditional, year-end bonus, known the as the "13th month."
The deficit was also caused by higher spending on personnel, including backdated worker contributions, the statement said.
The statement said the federal government's operational deficit, which includes debt costs, rose to 1.78 percent of GDP in the first 11 months of 1996 from 1.64 percent in the same period in 1995.

The drop in the January-November primary surplus was due principally to lower tax revenues from imported cars, which were hit by new tariffs; the effect in 1996 of pay rises awarded in September 1995; and social security deficits. Another factor was a 500 million reais advance from the federal government to the states to compensate for the exemption of exports from a so-called ICMS tax, it said.

The ministry document also noted a drop in the cost of real interest rates on the federal government's debt, which fell to 2.15 percent of GDP in the January-November period, down from 2.20 percent in the same period in 1995.
